topic: Microservices vs Modular Monolith for New Projects

post.topic: Microservices vs Modular Monolith for New Projects
post.linkedin_text:
Most new projects do not need microservices.

Yet teams still split their fresh architecture into six repositories on day one.

Here is what usually happens instead:

→ Network latency creeps into every simple read operation.
→ Distributed tracing becomes a full-time debugging chore.
→ Deployments turn into coordinated multi-repo nightmares.
→ Business logic fragments across half-finished API contracts.

A clean modular monolith gives you fast iteration, single-transaction guarantees, and painless local setups.

You can always extract independent services later when data boundaries actually demand it.

Where do you stand when kicking off a new system: start monolithic or go straight to distributed services?

Are we over-engineering day-one architectures?

Here is why the modular monolith usually wins early on:

⚡ Zero network latency between core domain modules
🛠 Simple local setup with zero Docker orchestration headaches

slides.title: Stop Building *Microservices* on Day One
slides.body: Why modular monoliths win for early-stage development speed.

slides.title: Debugging Is Dead Simple
slides.body: Trace bugs with standard stack traces in one repo instead of chasing distributed logs across multiple independent containers.

slides.title: ACID Transactions by Default
slides.body: Keep database consistency simple. You do not need two-phase commits or complex Saga patterns just to save linked records.

slides.title: Frictionless Refactoring
slides.body: When your domain model changes, refactoring function calls takes minutes. Changing network contracts across remote services breaks everything.

slides.title: Extract When Needed
slides.body: Build strict module boundaries inside your monolith today. If one module ever needs dedicated scaling, spin it out cleanly.
